drafted_from: workflow:possibility-to-proof's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its job, input schema and the step named in the worked example)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:possibility-to-proof on the idea: a weekly sourdough box that small cafes pre-order, for my bakery pursuit."
no_lists_because: It carries one idea through a hypothesis and a real test and keeps its observations in the run and in one linked record, so it ships no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Write the idea in a sentence (at least 3 characters), for example "a weekly sourdough box that small cafes pre-order", and add pursuit, context and authority (what the AI may do) when you have them.
2. Say "Run workflow:possibility-to-proof". At first-principles it names the decision the test would change, the chooser, the unmet need and a falsifiable before and after.

3. At combinatorics it finds the smallest mechanism from what exists; at test it picks a real-world test and writes predictions, baseline, success, failure and a resource ceiling before anything is observed.
4. At execute it carries out the authorized test and verifies every artifact where it lives; at learn-and-repeat it compares what happened with the predictions and sets the next test.

worked_examples.title: Define the decision, the chooser and what would prove the idea wrong
worked_examples.ask: Run workflow:possibility-to-proof: a weekly sourdough box that small cafes pre-order.

input.idea: A weekly sourdough box that small cafes pre-order

worked_examples.given: Read from tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json, step first-principles: its submit shape is decision, desired_change, chooser, need, evidence and falsifier, all text.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"decision":"Whether to bake a second weekly batch for cafe customers or keep baking only for walk-ins.","desired_change":"Five cafes each pre-order a weekly box (now: no cafe orders from us; wanted: 5 cafes repeat for 4 weeks).","chooser":"The cafe owner who buys the bread; the 12 cafes within two miles are reachable and represent the chooser.","need":"Cafes run out of fresh bread by Saturday noon and lose breakfast sales.","evidence":"Three cafe owners said they ran out last month; no one has paid yet.","falsifier":"If fewer than 3 of 12 cafes pay a deposit within 14 days, or fewer than 2 reorder in week 2, the idea is wrong."}
